tagline: From sampled data to filters, spectra, multirate systems, and deployable signal chains
audience: Busy engineers and technically mature programmers who want a first serious DSP course or a coherent return to material previously learned in fragments.
design_thesis: The course treats DSP as a sequence of representations that make an engineering decision possible. Samples and convolution establish exact time-domain behavior; complex exponentials, the DTFT, and the z-transform expose frequency response and stability; sampling and the DFT connect physical signals to finite computation; filter and multirate structures turn specifications into efficient systems; stochastic and short-time methods handle finite noisy data; audio and communications modules force the complete chain to survive real artifacts and implementation conventions.

course_prerequisites.requirement: Algebra and trigonometry, including geometric series, logarithms, radians, and manipulation of rational expressions.
course_prerequisites.honesty_note: These operations are used without remediation in transform, FFT, and filter derivations.

course_prerequisites.requirement: Complex arithmetic and Euler's identity at the level of rectangular/polar conversion and conjugation.
course_prerequisites.honesty_note: The course gives a visual re-anchoring in the first spectral lesson, but it is not a substitute for first exposure to complex numbers.

course_prerequisites.requirement: Single-variable calculus, including differentiation, integration, and the idea of convergence.
course_prerequisites.honesty_note: Continuous-time sampling arguments and analog-to-digital filter mappings use calculus; contour integration and measure theory are not required.

course_prerequisites.requirement: Elementary probability: mean, variance, covariance, and independent random variables.
course_prerequisites.honesty_note: The stochastic module reviews these objects for sequences but assumes the scalar ideas are familiar.

course_prerequisites.requirement: Ability to read and modify short Python/NumPy notebooks and interpret linear and logarithmic plots.
course_prerequisites.honesty_note: Applications are computational studies, not programming tutorials. No prior DSP or signals-and-systems course is assumed.

not_required: Optimization beyond linear algebra and the stated filter-design algorithms

outcomes.text: Analyze discrete-time signals and LTI systems in the time domain using sequence operations, impulse responses, convolution, and system properties.
Analyze LTI behavior with complex exponentials, the DTFT, frequency response, the z-transform, pole-zero geometry, causality, and stability.
Evaluate sampling rate, analog bandwidth, reconstruction, quantization, and dither choices for an acquisition system.
Compute and interpret DFT/FFT spectra with correct indexing, scaling, symmetry, windowing, leakage, and resolution judgments.
Design FIR and IIR filters from amplitude, phase, delay, and implementation specifications and realize them in numerically appropriate structures.
Design efficient decimators, interpolators, rational sample-rate converters, and analysis/synthesis filter banks using polyphase structures.
Evaluate power-spectral estimates for random finite records by reasoning about stationarity, bias, variance, leakage, resolution, and model mismatch.
Construct and validate short-time audio processing systems using STFT, overlap processing, reconstruction constraints, and phase-aware modification.
Construct a quadrature communications receiver that translates, selects, and detects a modulated channel while accounting for synchronization and interference.

Validate a DSP design against a real or reproducible artifact, state which ideal assumptions it uses, and diagnose departures caused by finite records, noise, rate, precision, or implementation conventions.

ordered_argument_spine.claim: A sampled signal is an indexed physical measurement, and elementary sequence operations are already useful when units, boundaries, and alignment remain explicit.
Linearity and time invariance make one impulse response predict every input through convolution.
Complex exponentials diagonalize LTI systems; the DTFT records their gains and phases, while the z-transform adds convergence, causality, and stability.
Sampling creates periodic spectral copies, so bandwidth and analog filtering—not later digital cleanup—decide whether the continuous signal remains identifiable.
The DFT is a finite sampling of a periodic spectrum, and FFT factorization makes it practical without changing what it means.
Finite observation changes the spectrum by convolution with a window, so reliable spectral claims require explicit leakage, resolution, amplitude, and noise-bandwidth budgets.
Filter design converts spectral requirements into coefficients, and realization converts algebraically equivalent transfer functions into systems with different delay, cost, and numerical risk.
Rate changes are filtering problems; polyphase identities remove computations that cannot affect retained outputs, and filter banks organize the same machinery into channels.
A spectrum estimated from random finite data is an estimator rather than a transform value, and every improvement trades resolution, variance, assumptions, or robustness.
Signals whose spectra change over time require local Fourier analysis and overlap reconstruction rather than one global spectrum.
Modulation is spectral translation; quadrature representation, filtering, and correlation turn that identity into a practical receiver.

polished_openers.rationale: The first two lessons require only arrays, units, multiplication, and addition. Each produces a complete visible result before any transform notation appears.

lessons.felt_win: The learner can read, align, shift, reverse, scale, and summarize a short sensor record without confusing sample index with physical time.
lessons.signature_experience: A synchronized strip chart and literal cell array update together as the learner applies delay, reversal, gain, and offset; the final task repairs an intentionally mislabeled plot.
lessons.polish_priority: Use one eight-sample accelerometer record, no abstract signals until every operation has a physical interpretation, and complete solutions for all boundary conventions.

lessons.felt_win: The learner manually computes and then verifies every output of a three-tap moving-average filter.
lessons.signature_experience: A five-frame figure sequence changes only the kernel alignment; cell products, their sum, and the output sample share color bindings. A short notebook reproduces the hand result.
lessons.polish_priority: Keep the first example causal and positive, then add one edge detector and one boundary near-miss so convolution is not mistaken for averaging.

core_vs_extra_policy.core_path: Forty-one core and synthesis lessons form a complete prerequisite graph and include every module application. Core lessons may contain optional starred proofs or derivations, but their main argument does not depend on them.
core_vs_extra_policy.extra_path: Four advanced lessons deepen design theory after the relevant core machinery is established. No core, synthesis, or later module lesson lists an extra lesson as a prerequisite.
extra_topics: Sinusoidal models and the phase vocoder

modules.title: Time-Domain Signals and LTI Systems
modules.argument_move: Start with literal sample arrays, derive convolution from a small filtering computation, then state the LTI conditions that make convolution universal.

lessons.title: Sampled Signals, Indices, and Units
lessons.goal: Analyze indexed signal records using physical units, alignment, delay, reversal, scaling, and offset.
key_ideas: Sample index is not physical time
Sequence operations require an explicit boundary convention
Amplitude units survive algebra and constrain interpretation

lessons.title: Convolution as a Sliding Dot Product
lessons.goal: Compute finite discrete convolution and interpret each output as a weighted local measurement.
key_ideas: Smoothing and differencing as two kernels

lessons.title: LTI Systems and Impulse Response
lessons.goal: Determine whether a system is linear and time invariant and derive its convolution representation from impulse decomposition.
key_ideas: Linearity and time invariance are separate tests
Impulse response determines an LTI system
Causality and BIBO stability in the time domain

lessons.title: Application: Sensor Smoothing and Event Detection
lessons.goal: Construct and validate a causal FIR chain that smooths a noisy sensor record while preserving detectable step events.

module_final_application.artifact: A reproducible accelerometer or industrial sensor trace with additive noise and labeled step events.
module_final_application.deliverable: A short FIR pipeline, hand-checked impulse response, plots before and after filtering, and quantitative false-alarm/delay measurements.
module_final_application.departure_from_ideal: The record is finite, startup state is unknown, measurement noise is not perfectly white, and smoothing delays and broadens the event being detected.

modules.title: Frequency-Domain LTI Systems and the z-Transform
modules.argument_move: Use rotating exponentials as LTI eigenfunctions, collect their gains in the DTFT, and extend the same expression into the z-plane to decide realizability and stability.

lessons.title: Complex Exponentials and Phasors
lessons.goal: Represent discrete sinusoids as rotating complex exponentials and relate frequency, phase, conjugation, and periodicity.

lessons.title: The Discrete-Time Fourier Transform
lessons.goal: Compute and interpret DTFTs using transform pairs, symmetry, shift, modulation, convolution, and Parseval relations.
key_ideas: Spectrum is a continuous periodic function of discrete frequency

lessons.title: Frequency Response, Phase, and Group Delay
lessons.goal: Predict sinusoidal and narrowband LTI outputs from magnitude, phase, phase delay, and group delay.
key_ideas: Phase controls alignment and waveform shape
Group delay tracks a narrowband envelope

lessons.title: z-Transform, Poles, Zeros, and Stability
lessons.goal: Analyze rational discrete-time systems using regions of convergence, pole-zero geometry, causality, and stability.
key_ideas: A transform expression needs a region of convergence
The unit circle yields the DTFT when it lies in the ROC
Causal stable rational systems have poles inside the unit circle

lessons.title: Application: DTMF Resonator Bank
lessons.goal: Construct and evaluate a stable resonator bank that identifies DTMF tones under duration, noise, and frequency-offset constraints.
key_ideas: Pole radius trades selectivity against settling time
Parallel channels implement a detector bank
Thresholds must reflect noise and finite tone duration

module_final_application.artifact: Recorded or synthesized telephone keypad tones with leading/trailing silence, noise, and modest oscillator error.
module_final_application.deliverable: A stable detector bank, pole-zero and response plots, confusion results, and a justified radius/threshold choice.
module_final_application.departure_from_ideal: Real tones are finite, may be detuned, pass through an unknown channel, and do not reach steady-state resonator amplitude instantly.

modules.title: Sampling and Data Conversion
modules.argument_move: Derive sampling as multiplication by an impulse train, make aliasing irreversible spectral overlap, and add amplitude quantization to form an honest acquisition budget.

lessons.title: Sampling as Spectral Replication
lessons.goal: Derive the spectrum of an impulse-sampled continuous-time signal and map continuous frequency to discrete frequency.
key_ideas: Ω=ωT maps physical to discrete frequency

lessons.title: Aliasing, Reconstruction, and Anti-Alias Filtering
lessons.goal: Evaluate whether a bandlimited signal can be reconstructed and specify the analog anti-alias filter required before sampling.
key_ideas: Aliased components cannot be separated after sampling
Ideal sinc reconstruction is a limiting model

lessons.title: Quantization, Dither, and Converter Budgets
lessons.goal: Evaluate bit depth and dither choices from dynamic-range, overload, and error-model requirements.
key_ideas: Step size and overload are separate failure modes
Bit depth determines a finite amplitude budget

lessons.title: Application: Audio Acquisition Chain
lessons.goal: Specify and test an audio acquisition chain from analog bandwidth through anti-alias filtering, sample rate, quantization, and dither.

module_final_application.artifact: A speech/music excerpt containing near-Nyquist content and a low-level fade, passed through a simulated ADC front end.
module_final_application.deliverable: An anti-alias specification, sample-rate and bit-depth justification, aliased/clean spectra, and a listening/measurement comparison with and without dither.
module_final_application.departure_from_ideal: The analog filter is finite order, converter noise is not exactly independent or uniform, clocks jitter, and audio bandwidth is a system choice rather than a universal constant.

modules.title: DFT, FFT, and Finite-Record Spectra
modules.argument_move: Connect the finite DFT to the DTFT and periodic extension, factor its computation, then show how the observation window—not the FFT call—sets spectral evidence.

lessons.title: DFT Definition, Symmetry, and Scaling
lessons.goal: Compute and interpret the DFT as frequency samples of a finite record's periodic extension using consistent indexing and normalization.

lessons.title: Radix-2 FFT Factorization
lessons.goal: Derive and trace a radix-2 FFT, including butterflies, twiddle factors, operation count, and bit-reversed ordering.
key_ideas: Factorization changes cost, not the transform

lessons.title: Finite Records, Leakage, and Window Metrics
lessons.goal: Evaluate window choices using main-lobe width, sidelobe behavior, coherent gain, scalloping loss, and equivalent noise bandwidth.
key_ideas: Finite observation is time multiplication and spectral convolution
Every taper trades resolution and leakage

lessons.title: Spectral Resolution, Zero Padding, and Calibration
lessons.goal: Evaluate whether a finite-record spectrum supports claims about tone frequency, amplitude, separation, and noise level.
key_ideas: Zero padding interpolates without adding information
One-sided spectra need explicit amplitude scaling
ENBW converts bin power to noise density
Phase and tone placement bias peaks

lessons.title: Application: Weak-Tone Spectrum Analyzer
lessons.goal: Construct and validate an FFT analyzer that detects a weak sinusoid near a stronger off-bin interferer.
key_ideas: Window selection from a detection requirement

module_final_application.artifact: A reproducible version of Harris's unequal-tone experiment: a weak line roughly 40 dB below a nearby strong line, with the strong tone shifted on and off the DFT grid.
module_final_application.deliverable: A tested analyzer configuration, fixed-axis window comparison, detection decision, amplitude-error table, and latency/dynamic-range justification.
module_final_application.departure_from_ideal: Real analyzers face oscillator drift, nonstationary interference, ADC noise, and window-dependent threshold statistics rather than two eternal sinusoids.

modules.title: FIR and IIR Filter Design and Realization
modules.argument_move: Translate frequency-domain tolerances into FIR and IIR coefficients, then treat implementation structure and finite precision as part of the design rather than an afterthought.

lessons.title: FIR Specifications and Windowed-Sinc Design
lessons.goal: Design a causal linear-phase FIR filter from passband, stopband, transition-width, ripple, and delay specifications using a windowed ideal response.
key_ideas: Ideal lowpass sinc is infinite and noncausal
Window main lobe maps to transition width

lessons.title: Equiripple and Least-Squares FIR Design
lessons.goal: Design a weighted equiripple or least-squares FIR filter from the error criterion implied by a specification.

lessons.title: FIR Structures and Fast Convolution
lessons.goal: Select a direct, folded linear-phase, or FFT-block FIR realization from latency, throughput, memory, and coefficient constraints.
key_ideas: Direct and FFT convolution have different crossovers
Block size trades latency and throughput

lessons.title: IIR Prototypes and Bilinear Design
lessons.goal: Design a digital IIR filter by selecting an analog prototype, prewarping critical frequencies, and applying the bilinear transform.

lessons.title: IIR Sections and Numerical Robustness
lessons.goal: Evaluate scaled second-order-section realizations against quantization, overflow, roundoff, and limit-cycle risks.
key_ideas: Equivalent transfer functions are not numerically equivalent
Pole-zero pairing and section order matter
Fixed-point feedback can sustain limit cycles

lessons.title: Minimum-Phase, Allpass, and Hilbert Structures
lessons.goal: Analyze magnitude-equivalent systems using minimum-phase factors, allpass sections, Hilbert transformers, and analytic-signal construction.

lessons.title: Application: ECG Filter Chain
lessons.goal: Design and compare FIR and IIR filters that remove baseline drift, mains interference, and high-frequency noise from an ECG while preserving waveform timing.
key_ideas: Zero-phase offline filtering versus causal deployment

module_final_application.artifact: An openly available ECG segment with baseline drift, a narrow mains component, and broadband measurement noise, or a reproducible contamination of a clean trace.
module_final_application.deliverable: Two specification-compliant FIR/IIR chains, response and pole-zero checks, waveform-distortion metrics, and a deployment recommendation for offline versus real-time use.
module_final_application.departure_from_ideal: ECG morphology is nonstationary, interference frequency drifts, forward-reverse filtering is noncausal, and a mathematically sharp filter can distort clinically relevant timing.

modules.title: Multirate Processing and Filter Banks
modules.argument_move: Show how downsampling and upsampling move spectral copies, design the filters that prevent overlap and imaging, then restructure them so arithmetic occurs at the lowest useful rate.

lessons.title: Downsampling, Upsampling, and Spectral Images
lessons.goal: Analyze decimation and interpolation in time and frequency and identify aliasing and imaging conditions.
key_ideas: Upsampling inserts zeros and creates images
Rate annotations are part of every block diagram

lessons.title: Rational Sample-Rate Conversion
lessons.goal: Design an L/M sample-rate converter and distribute its transition and attenuation requirements across one or more stages.
key_ideas: One filter suppresses images and aliases

lessons.title: Polyphase Decomposition and Noble Identities
lessons.goal: Derive polyphase rate-converter structures that avoid operations on discarded samples and inserted zeros.
key_ideas: Polyphase decomposition partitions coefficients by residue class
Noble identities move filters across rate changers
Arithmetic belongs at the low rate

lessons.title: Perfect-Reconstruction Filter Banks
lessons.goal: Analyze a two-channel critically sampled analysis/synthesis bank and verify alias cancellation and delayed perfect reconstruction.
key_ideas: Perfect reconstruction up to gain and delay

lessons.title: Paraunitary and Wavelet Filter Banks
lessons.goal: Analyze paraunitary, cosine-modulated, and dyadic wavelet banks as structured perfect-reconstruction systems.

lessons.title: Application: Subband Audio Coder
lessons.goal: Construct and evaluate a critically sampled audio subband coder with unequal quantization and polyphase implementation.

module_final_application.artifact: A short music or speech recording encoded by a two- or four-band analysis/synthesis bank with controlled subband quantization.
module_final_application.deliverable: A reconstructing unquantized bank, rate/operation counts, two bit-allocation policies, objective error spectra, and listening comparisons.
module_final_application.departure_from_ideal: Quantization breaks perfect reconstruction, real filters have delay and finite stopbands, and perceptual importance is not captured by equal mean-square error alone.

modules.title: Stochastic Spectral Analysis
modules.argument_move: Replace the deterministic spectrum of one known sequence by statistical descriptions and estimators, then make every smooth-looking curve account for its bias, variance, and assumptions.

lessons.title: Random Sequences, Autocorrelation, and Power Spectral Density
lessons.goal: Derive and interpret autocorrelation and PSD for wide-sense stationary sequences and their LTI-filtered outputs.
key_ideas: PSD is the DTFT of autocorrelation
White means uncorrelated across nonzero lags
LTI output PSD is |H|² times input PSD

lessons.title: Periodogram and Welch Spectral Estimation
lessons.goal: Design a nonparametric PSD estimate and evaluate its leakage, bias, variance, overlap, and resolution.
key_ideas: A periodogram is noisy even for long records
Windowing smooths and biases the estimate
Overlap does not create independent records
Welch trades segment length for stability

lessons.title: Autoregressive Spectral Models
lessons.goal: Evaluate an autoregressive spectral model using Yule-Walker equations, prediction error, and order checks.
key_ideas: AR spectra are rational all-pole models
Yule-Walker links covariance to prediction coefficients
Model order changes resolution and variance
Stable poles and residual whiteness are validation checks

lessons.title: Subspace Line-Spectrum Estimation
lessons.goal: Analyze MUSIC and ESPRIT frequency estimates using signal/noise subspaces, rank, model order, and array or time-series geometry.
key_ideas: Sensitivity to order and coherent sources

lessons.title: Application: Vibration Spectrum Monitor
lessons.goal: Construct a vibration-monitoring spectrum estimate that separates rotating lines from broadband noise and reports uncertainty across repeated records.
key_ideas: Confidence through repeatability and sensitivity analysis

module_final_application.artifact: A measured or reproducibly simulated rotating-machine vibration record with shaft harmonics, changing broadband noise, and finite observation intervals.
module_final_application.deliverable: A Welch monitor, AR comparison, sensitivity sweep over segment length/window/model order, and a fault-line decision with uncertainty and false-peak diagnostics.
module_final_application.departure_from_ideal: Machine speed drifts, vibration is cyclostationary, sensor mounting colors the spectrum, and neither Gaussian noise nor a low-order AR model is guaranteed.

modules.title: Short-Time Audio Processing
modules.argument_move: Localize Fourier analysis in time, preserve linear convolution and overlap reconstruction, then modify spectra without treating phase and transients as disposable.

lessons.title: Short-Time Fourier Transform and Spectrograms
lessons.goal: Construct and interpret an STFT using window length, FFT length, hop size, and time-frequency resolution appropriate to a changing signal.
key_ideas: A spectrogram is a sequence of local spectra
Window length trades time against frequency localization
Speech harmonics and formants need different resolutions

lessons.title: FFT Convolution and Overlap Processing
lessons.goal: Construct overlap-add and overlap-save systems that perform long linear convolution with bounded latency and correct boundary handling.
key_ideas: Circular convolution requires padding or overlap
Block size determines cost and latency

lessons.title: WOLA Reconstruction and Spectral Modification
lessons.goal: Design a weighted overlap-add analysis/modification/synthesis system and verify reconstruction, phase consistency, and transient behavior.
key_ideas: STFT as a modulated filter bank
Spectral changes can break alias cancellation
Transient smearing is a model failure

lessons.title: Sinusoidal Models and the Phase Vocoder
lessons.goal: Analyze sinusoidal tracking and phase-vocoder time scaling using instantaneous frequency, phase continuation, and transient-aware reconstruction.
key_ideas: Time scaling conflicts with inter-bin phase
Tones, noise, and transients need different models

lessons.title: Application: Speech Spectral Denoiser
lessons.goal: Construct and evaluate a real-time STFT speech denoiser that estimates a noise floor, applies a bounded gain mask, and reconstructs without frame artifacts.

module_final_application.artifact: A noisy speech recording containing a noise-only calibration interval, voiced/unvoiced segments, and at least one transient consonant.
module_final_application.deliverable: A WOLA denoiser, reconstruction null test, time-frequency mask plots, SNR or segmental metrics, latency calculation, and listening comparison across two parameter settings.
module_final_application.departure_from_ideal: Noise is not perfectly stationary, speech and noise spectra overlap, isolated-bin attenuation creates musical noise, and a mathematically valid overlap condition does not guarantee perceptual transparency.

modules.title: Communications Signal Processing
modules.argument_move: Represent real passbands by complex baseband, use multiplication for spectral translation, then combine channel filters, synchronization, and correlation into a receiver whose failures are measurable.

lessons.title: Analytic Signals and I/Q Representation
lessons.goal: Represent a real bandpass signal as complex baseband and relate analytic signals, Hilbert pairs, positive frequency, and I/Q imbalance.
key_ideas: Complex envelopes separate carrier from modulation
I and Q are orthogonal projections
Gain and phase imbalance create image leakage

lessons.title: Modulation, Mixing, and Channel Selection
lessons.goal: Design a sampled frequency-translation and channel-selection chain with correct image, alias, filter, and oscillator budgets.
key_ideas: Channel filters and decimation form a digital downconverter

lessons.title: Matched Detection and Synchronization
lessons.goal: Construct a matched-filter detector and evaluate timing and carrier-phase errors in additive noise.
key_ideas: Correlation is convolution with a reversed conjugate template
The matched filter maximizes sampled SNR for white noise
Timing offset moves the correlation peak
Carrier phase error attenuates coherent detection

lessons.title: Application: Software AM Receiver
lessons.goal: Construct and validate a software AM receiver that tunes one channel from a sampled band, rejects adjacent interference, demodulates audio, and reports synchronization limits.

module_final_application.artifact: A recorded or reproducibly synthesized complex-IQ AM band containing a desired speech channel, an adjacent interferer, noise, carrier offset, and I/Q imbalance.
module_final_application.deliverable: A tuned and decimated receiver, spectral plots at each stage, recovered audio, adjacent-channel and noise measurements, and comparison of envelope and coherent detection.
module_final_application.departure_from_ideal: Oscillators are offset, channels are not perfectly bandlimited, front ends have I/Q imbalance, interference is time varying, and coherent detection requires phase information an envelope detector avoids at a power cost.

research_trace.role: Rigorous backbone for sequences, LTI systems, DTFT/z-transform, DFT, structures, sampling, FIR/IIR design, and finite-word caveats.
Engineer-facing numerical examples, implementation conventions, FFT interpretation, FIR/IIR tradeoffs, quadrature, multirate structures, and practical failure modes.
Authoritative derivations of rate-change spectra, noble identities, polyphase systems, perfect reconstruction, paraunitary banks, and subband quantization.
Open computational backbone for convolution, transforms, filter design, converter experiments, smoothing, multirate systems, and implementation-oriented exercises.

research_trace.source: The Scientist and Engineer's Guide to Digital Signal Processing
research_trace.role: Low-floor opening sequence, physical intuition, array-first convolution, practical filters, numerical judgment, and application-led explanations.
Representation-first dependency order, transform and sampling derivations, DTMF/ECG/audio-CD/radio applications, and prediction-before-solution problem design.

research_trace.source: The Fourier Transform and Its Applications, EE 261
research_trace.role: Mathematical bridge for Fourier projection, transform dualities, convolution, sampling, DFT indexing, FFT, and normalization discipline.
Graduate-level ordering, counterexamples, structure and numerical-equivalence distinctions, spectral-analysis misconceptions, multirate projects, and STFT/filter-bank unification.
Stochastic spectral definitions, periodogram/Welch bias-variance analysis, AR/Yule-Walker models, MUSIC/ESPRIT, model-order issues, and measured-data studies.
Window calibration, audio spectral resolution, Welch estimation, STFT/WOLA, filter-bank duality, phase-aware modification, and executable audio applications.

research_trace.source: On the Use of Windows for Harmonic Analysis with the Discrete Fourier Transform
research_trace.role: Canonical finite-record conventions, leakage mechanisms, ENBW/scalloping/processing-loss metrics, and the unequal-tone detection experiment.

research_trace.source: An Algorithm for the Machine Calculation of Complex Fourier Series
research_trace.role: Primary-source FFT factorization, operation-count argument, in-place butterflies, data ordering, and architecture-sensitive radix choice.

research_trace.source: Seeing Circles, Sines, and Signals: A Compact Primer on Digital Signal Processing
research_trace.role: Visual coordination of phasors, sample dots, basis products, complex coefficients, alias families, DFT bins, zero padding, and leakage; its informal claims require the boundary qualifications supplied by the rigorous sources.

assessment_and_pacing.lesson_pattern: One substantive objective per 30–50 minute core lesson, with a concrete computation before the general form where it exposes the need; worked-example/problem pairs occur in the body, followed by mixed exercises and references.
assessment_and_pacing.retrieval: From lesson 3 onward, each lesson opens with two to four prerequisite prompts; each module application mixes at least three earlier techniques without naming which one applies.
assessment_and_pacing.applications: Each module ends with a runnable study or deployed-system analogue, a numerical acceptance criterion, and an explicit idealization audit.
assessment_and_pacing.busy_engineer_route: Complete the 41 core/synthesis lessons in order. Each module can be taken as a two-week unit with one concept lesson and one worked block per sitting; all four extra lessons are optional and non-blocking.
assessment_and_pacing.proof_depth: Core identities are derived far enough to support design decisions. Longer convergence proofs, paraunitary constructions, optimal-window theory, and subspace-estimator asymptotics remain starred or extra.
